source.title: Minimum Cost to Acquire Required Items

teaching.hint: After fixing one item count, where can the expression for the remaining cost change?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Fixing the count of combined items leaves independent deficits; their cost is a piecewise-linear function with breakpoints when each requirement becomes saturated.
solution_outline.approach: Evaluate total cost with zero combined items, with min(need1,need2) combined items, and with max(need1,need2) combined items. For each choice, cover any remaining deficits by the corresponding single-type items and choose the cheapest total.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: For a chosen combined count b, the exact least cost is b*costBoth plus each positive remaining requirement times its single cost.
solution_outline.correctness: The cost function is linear between zero and the smaller demand, and between the two demands. Each interval therefore has a minimum at an endpoint. Beyond the larger demand, extra combined items only add positive cost. The three tested endpoints consequently contain a global optimum, including deliberate overbuying for the smaller side.
solution_outline.complexity: `O(1)` time and auxiliary space. Costs can reach `10^15` and need corresponding integer range.
solution_outline.pitfall: Limiting combined purchases to the smaller demand misses cases where they are cheaper even for supplying only the larger requirement.

source_fidelity_notes: Made extra units and unlimited supply explicit; retained zero demands, positive costs, and large count bounds.
common_wrong_turns: Limiting combined purchases to the smaller demand misses cases where they are cheaper even for supplying only the larger requirement.
